items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: trying to learn how to play like Teddy Wilson

ctx.x: My mother was. See, my father died when I was three months old. So I never had a father. I had a stepfather. And he was very un-musical. He wanted me to do all kinds of things that I didn't want to do, like caddie for him every Sunday, when I was a... I was a tennis player, and I don't mind saying I was a good one, and I won a few tournaments in my time up there. But on Sundays, when all the good players were playing, I was out on the golf course carrying his clubs. And he was a dubber. And we never really had…

So when I finally got to be twenty-one years old, he was sending me to law school; he was going to make a lawyer out of me. And I had been practicing, trying to learn how to play like Teddy Wilson. And when I got to be twenty-one years old, I just said, with the help of my wife, who I was
